title: Choose LuxeGlow's visual world
question: The lead explores a beauty-packaging world; my recommendation connects treatment swatches directly to the appointment ledger. Choose one, adopt an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Dieline Vanity Counter
options.lineage: beauty packaging dielines and mirrored vanity trays
options.thesis: Every service and appointment becomes a precisely folded salon object nested in one working vanity counter.
options.viewport: An asymmetrical salon counter pairs one decisive Astrid image with die-cut service panels; a booking ticket tab stays visible beside real prices and durations.
options.risk: It becomes generic cosmetics luxury if the folding system does not carry scheduling, status, and admin work.

raised.raise: The booking journey unfolds panel by panel while keeping prior choices visible.
One bold negative-space cut gives the first viewport a memorable silhouette instead of another card grid.
Date and time states visibly mature from available to held to confirmed.
Price, duration, capacity, and status remain numerically exact.

options.label: Swatch-to-Ledger Counter
options.lineage: treatment swatch fans and the front-desk carbon appointment ledger
options.thesis: A customer's treatment swatches become the same appointment ticket that customers and staff track together.
options.viewport: A tactile swatch fan introduces real treatments beside a crisp appointment-ledger strip showing price, duration, open Lucena booking times, and one stamped primary action.
options.risk: Paper and lacquer can become faux-skeuomorphic or cluttered unless controls stay crisp and native.

options.label: Lucena Timetable Rack
options.lineage: a 1970s pocket timetable rendered as raked tinted-glass slides
options.thesis: Services, open slots, and booking status become one continuous rack of time-aware salon information.
options.viewport: Raked slides move from treatment to available time to appointment reference; one type size forces hierarchy through weight, reversal, and rules.
options.case: It matches the scheduling mechanism exceptionally well, but customers identify less immediately with transit graphics than with salon swatches.
options.risk: It can feel technical or transport-themed unless salon imagery and treatment content remain unmistakable.

options.label: Photocopied J-card
options.thesis: The salon journey unfolds like a numbered photocopied sleeve.
options.viewport: A hand-numbered fold moves through treatment, time, and confirmation.
options.case: It loses both audience identification and premium service clarity.
options.kept: Sequential folding gives the lead direction a stronger booking reveal.
options.risk: It reads underground and handmade rather than polished and trustworthy.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.lineage: surreal weather blocks cut into temporary architecture
options.thesis: Treatments are carved from soft atmospheric blocks and assembled into a visit.
options.viewport: A salon photograph is cut by deep blue voids and stacked treatment blocks.
options.case: It loses both salon recognition and booking clarity.
options.kept: A bolder use of negative space raises the lead's first-viewport silhouette.
options.risk: The metaphor overwhelms real services and becomes expensive decorative theater.

options.label: Seasonal Jar Calendar
options.lineage: pickling jars that make time and maturation visible
options.thesis: Appointment states mature through clear dated vessels.
options.viewport: Dated vessels track open, held, and confirmed times on a vertical shelf.
options.case: The time metaphor is legible, but the culinary world misidentifies the product.
options.kept: Time and status should visibly progress instead of changing only a badge.
options.risk: It reads as food or wellness retail, not a salon booking system.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: The entire salon experience lives inside one breathing field of lacquer color.
options.viewport: One oversized Astrid wordmark floats over a reactive full-screen field.
options.case: It sacrifices direct service comparison and booking clarity for atmosphere.
options.kept: One authored motion moment is stronger than many scattered hover effects.
options.risk: Performance cost and low information density make it unsuitable for daily operations.

options.label: Nixie Appointment Counter
options.lineage: glass laboratory counters with physically layered digits
options.thesis: Every price, duration, slot, and status arrives as a precise physical count.
options.viewport: Appointment quantities glow above a compact treatment panel.
options.case: Precision supports the product, but the laboratory language has weak salon identification.
options.kept: All operational numbers remain exact, aligned, and visibly stateful.
options.risk: It feels industrial, dark, and masculine in a way the service mix does not justify.

canonCard.label: Soft Luxury Salon
canonCard.thesis: The familiar cream, blush, plum, gold, rounded-card salon site executed with exceptional restraint.
canonCard.viewport: A split hero introduces the salon beside a photo collage, booking CTA, service cards, and review proof.
canonCard.risk: It is immediately understandable but deliberately indistinguishable from many competing beauty sites.
